1. Parallel convs at a shared sum node add up. If false, a conv sibling makes a second conv redundant, so the edit gains less.
2. A skip edge only helps optimization and never competes with convs. If false, a skip sibling at node 3 changes how much a conv edit adds.
3. Pooling upstream is a harmless, neutral parent. If false, pooling blurs features, so a 3x3 conv downstream is redundant while a 1x1 conv is complementary.
4. Deeper conv chains always compound receptive field. If false, a conv parent saturates capacity and the downstream conv gains less.
5. Kernel size matters independently of the parent. If false, the 3x3 and 1x1 edits behave oppositely under a pool or skip parent.
6. Edges feeding different nodes are independent. If false, a downstream skip or pool changes the value of an upstream conv.
7. A direct 0->3 route never reduces the value of the deep path. If false, a direct skip or conv bypass changes what the chain adds.
8. Effects are the same across datasets. This is not negated here, since each hypothesis must hold on all three datasets.
